purpose: BOM-21's benchmark tasks (pre-registration 7). Hand-curated 2026-10-28: one volume per novel from a period edition (no modern reprints, which carry the original date: ids with isbn_, 0000 or bwb_ are excluded), dates checked against BOM-56's title-page verdicts.

federalist.note: political essays; the history controls are the nearest registered genre

pseudo_biblical.note: imposters must not be the task authors' own works or copies of them

dictated.author: scott
dictated.tests_note: Tales of My Landlord, Third Series (Edinburgh, 1821 printing of the 1819 text), volumes 1-2 (The Bride of Lammermoor) and 4 (A Legend of Montrose), which Scott dictated to William Laidlaw and John Ballantyne during his illness of 1819 (Lockhart, Memoirs of the Life of Sir Walter Scott, ch. 43). Volume 3 holds the end of one and the start of the other and is left out. Checked by character names: vol 1-2 Ravenswood 193/283, vol 4 Dalgetty 194.
dictated.reference_note: Scott's references are novels he wrote by hand (Guy Mannering 1815, Rob Roy 1818, Kenilworth 1821, Peveril of the Peak 1823, Quentin Durward 1823, Redgauntlet 1824); Ivanhoe, partly dictated, is left out. The other novelists are his contemporaries, with the Scots (Galt, Hogg, Ferrier) as the hardest competition.
